Diploperennis with partner taxa in its union: dosage and fragmentation

chr10 GENOTYPE runs alone (1270808), D (+ parviglumis), E (+ mexicana), F (+ both); 2026-10-16

Author

Fausto Rodríguez-Zapata

Published

October 16, 2026

Why

User, 2026-10-16: “plan the same approach for diplo as we did for huehue: make the genotyping using information from parviglumis and mexicana; there is a chance that the fragmentation improves; judging by the FST it should work”; then, for this notebook, the effect of partner taxa in the union on dosage and fragmentation. Run plan: docs/runs/genotype_diploperennis_partners_chr10.md. Runs shown: alone, D, E.

Inputs (not in git): small tables in diplo_partners/, made by agent/diplo_chr10/collect.sh and agent/nb08/collect.sh (logs there) and the measurement jobs (agent/diplo_chr10/measure_diplo_*.log); master copy in /rsstu/users/r/rrellan/BZea/ZEAL/genotype/notebook_inputs/diplo_partners/; copy it next to this notebook to re-render.

4. Chromosome painting

5. Notes (2026-10-16)

  • Partners add candidates, not markers: the union grows 2-2.5-fold; each donor takes only the sites its own BC1 reads support.
  • Noise and fragmentation change little for diploperennis: its own 6-donor union already supplies gap markers; partners lower the gap markers’ REF noise by at most half a point, and trim the most fragmented samples (maximum segments down by 2-4) while medians stay at 0-3. Samples with REF % ALT > 3 stay flagged.
  • Dosage: class shares barely move; ALT segments read less ALT in Zd.0010_P2 and Zd.0040_P1 with partners (gap markers there read 67-72 % ALT against 80-91 % at own markers): a slide toward HET, larger with mexicana.
  • The fragmentation measure does not move: the share of SNP50K HET segments >= 1 Mb kept whole or split into >= 3 pieces changes by a few points at most, in either direction. In the painting, Zd.0020_P3 is fragmented in every union where SNP50K calls long HET segments: its fragmentation has another cause than marker density (the diagnosis’s dilution in its pools is the candidate).
  • D and E agree closely: the partner’s taxon matters less than adding one.
  • Run F (both partners) to be added when it finishes.
